name: Meenakshi Raman
headline: 73, field associate for a university ethnobotany study, Kodaikanal
title: The Offer to Join the Evening Gathering
situation: After a morning walk with the university team, Meenakshi stops at the well to wash her hands. Her old neighbor, Kamakshi, is there and tells her that the women of the village now meet on Thursday evenings at the temple hall to swap remedies and tell stories about the healers they knew. Kamakshi asks Meenakshi to come, saying, 'Everyone wants to hear your knowledge.' Meenakshi is used to working alone at dawn, and she feels shy about sitting with women her own age who might expect her to lead. She has not joined such a gathering for years.

context.relationship_profiles:
Kamakshi has been her neighbor for over forty years; they exchange vegetables and news but have never sat together at temple gatherings.
The other village women treat Meenakshi with respect because of her university work, but she has kept herself apart from their daily circles.
Her own daughters are married and visit rarely; she has not told them how much the forest work means to her.
context.tendencies:
When her children were young, she stayed home rather than join the temple women's groups, saying her work would wait for no one.
She has twice declined invitations from the anganwadi worker to lead health talks, preferring to teach one healer at a time.
In the university team, she speaks up about authorship, but in village company she waits for someone to ask her directly.
context.current_state:
She is tired but satisfied after the morning walk, her hands still cold from the well water.
Her mind is full of the plant names she recorded, and she feels the familiar shyness that comes when Kamakshi calls her by name.
She is slightly hungry and worried about the time, because she still has to prepare lunch before the afternoon heat.
context.immediate_memories:
Kamakshi's phrase 'Everyone wants to hear your knowledge' brings back the last time she stood at the temple hall, at her youngest son's wedding, where she sat in a corner and said little.
The sight of the temple hall reminds her of the Thursday satsang she used to attend years ago, until her husband fell ill and she stopped going.
Kamakshi's voice reminds her of the time Kamakshi's mother shared buttermilk with her at this same well, after Meenakshi's first child was born.
context.reflective_memories:
When she taught herself to read at forty-two, she practiced alone in the kitchen at night, hiding the notebook from relatives; she learned best without an audience.
Her mother used to say that healing knowledge is passed woman to woman in quiet voices, not in front of a crowd.
She has seen younger villagers laugh at old remedies as superstition, so she has grown used to keeping her knowledge close until she is sure it will be heard.
